source_text: Non temere hic ordo servatur. Prius enim corrigenda est vita, deinde discenda natura rerum, ut tandem mens purgata Deum contempletur. Qui sine morum correctione ad contemplationem irruit, in errorem cadit. Ideo Salomon pueris et incipientibus Proverbia, proficientibus Ecclesiasten, perfectis Canticum Canticorum dispensavit.
pass_a_gloss: Not rashly this order is-kept. First indeed to-be-corrected is life, then to-be-learned nature of-things, that at-last mind purged God may-contemplate...
pass_b_english: This order is not kept by chance. First life must be corrected, then the nature of things learned, so that at last a purged mind may contemplate God. Whoever rushes at contemplation without correction of morals falls into error. Therefore Solomon dispensed Proverbs to children and beginners, Ecclesiastes to those making progress, and the Song of Songs to the perfect.
